title: AC Feasibility Prompts Schema
description: Schema for .claude/metadata/ac-feasibility-prompts.json — externalized LLM-readable prompt block driving the AC verification-mechanism feasibility gate in /add-story, /bug, /enhancement (and, per #2425 follow-up, /create-prd and /create-backlog).

version.description: Schema version of this prompts file. Bump on breaking shape changes.

classify.description: First gate: classify each AC as deliverable vs verification.

verificationGate.description: Second gate: for verification ACs, name the mechanism explicitly and check existing test-harness usage.

triggerPhrases.description: Heuristic phrases that flag an AC for verificationGate evaluation. The list is intentionally non-exhaustive — the load-bearing piece is the gate's prompts, not the trigger list. Add phrases as new aspirational-mechanism patterns emerge.

deliverableSplit.description: Third gate: when an AC bundles deliverable + verification, split into independently judgable ACs. Applies to story ACs AND to epic success criteria (#2508) — an epic criterion bundling a satisfied deliverable with an unsatisfiable verification cannot be expressed by one checkbox.

appliesTo.description: Authoring surfaces this gate must be applied to. Epic success criteria were omitted until #2508.

phaseFeasibility.description: Fourth gate (#2508): can this AC close inside the workflow phase that owns it? verificationGate asks whether a mechanism exists; this asks whether the condition can resolve before the story reaches in_review. An AC whose condition resolves later deadlocks the gh pmu checkbox gate.

gatePhases.description: Phase tokens permitted in the → GATE: annotation. Kept narrow on purpose — every token widens the Step 4b force-move exemption.

annotationFormat.description: Mirrors the annotationFormat in .claude/scripts/shared/lib/qa-config.json. The box stays unchecked by design; the annotation is what distinguishes an intentionally-open gate from unfinished work.

triggerPhrases.description: Heuristic phrases flagging an AC for phase evaluation. Non-exhaustive — the gate's question applies to every AC regardless of trigger match.

ownedElsewhere.description: Release-phase work already discharged by another command's checklist. This class is dropped at authoring, NOT annotated — a story checkbox would duplicate an obligation another command already owns and create a second place to mark it done.

ownerChecklistItem.description: Verbatim checklist line in the owning command spec. Must exist there — the claim is verified by test, so this file cannot itself name a capability a command lacks.

dischargedByWorkflow.description: Fifth gate (#3316): ACs restating a check a /work step already runs on every issue. Not a phase class — the condition resolves during implementation — so it sits beside phaseFeasibility, not inside it. Dropped at authoring like ownedElsewhere, but with no ownerChecklistItem: the owner is a rule step, which has no checklist line to quote.

owner.description: The /work step that discharges the AC.

examples.description: AC wordings of this class. Non-exhaustive — judge by what the AC asks for, not its wording.

keptWhen.description: When the owner step runs nothing, so the AC is not redundant and must be kept.
